description:
As a platform engineer, you need to ensure that the current release of your CI/CD pipeline is always pointed to by a consistent symbolic link. There is a new deployment directory for the latest release at /home/user/deployments/release_2.1.0 and an existing symbolic link at /home/user/deployments/current (which currently points to an old release directory). Update the symbolic link so that /home/user/deployments/current points to /home/user/deployments/release_2.1.0. After updating the symbolic link, create a log file at /home/user/deployments/symlink_update.log containing exactly one line with the following format (all lowercase): 
symlink updated: current now points to release_2.1.0
This log file will be checked for both the exact line above and its correct location. Do not include any extra characters, and be sure the symbolic link is updated correctly. The verification will check both the symbolic link and the log file contents.
truth:
Before the task starts:
- /home/user/deployments/ exists.
- /home/user/deployments/release_2.1.0/ exists and can be pointed to.
- /home/user/deployments/current is a symbolic link that points to an old release directory, e.g., /home/user/deployments/release_2.0.5.

Final state:
- /home/user/deployments/current is a symbolic link that points to /home/user/deployments/release_2.1.0.
- /home/user/deployments/symlink_update.log exists and contains exactly:
symlink updated: current now points to release_2.1.0
(with a single line, no trailing whitespace or newline characters beyond the end of this line).
